record.context_brief: Stability of a dimension estimate under bounded perturbations
record.original_question: Let S: X → Y and T: Y → Z be closed operators, and let A: X → Y and B: Y → Z be bounded operators. Define S̃ = S + A and T̃ = T + B. It is known, when X, Y, and Z are Hilbert spaces, that dim N(T̃)/R(S̃) = dim N(T)/R(S) < ∞. Does the same estimate remain valid when X, Y, and Z are Banach spaces instead of Hilbert spaces?

evidence.quote: Given closed operators S: X → Y, T: Y → Z and bounded operators A: X → Y, B: Y → Z. Let S̃ = S + A, T̃ = T + B. Known that dim N(T̃) / R(S̃)=dim N(T) / R(S)<∞ if X, Y, Z are Hilbert spaces. Does the same estimate hold if X, Y, Z are Banach spaces?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$, $Y$, $Z$ be Banach spaces. Let $S\colon X	o Y$ and $T\colon Y	o Z$ be closed (not necessarily bounded) linear operators with domains $\mathcal{D}(S)\subseteq X$ and $\mathcal{D}(T)\subseteq Y$, and assume that $R(S)\subseteq \mathcal{D}(T)$ and $TS=0$, so that the quotient $N(T)/R(S)$ is well defined, where $N(T)=\{y\in\mathcal{D}(T):Ty=0\}$ and $R(S)=\{Sx:x\in\mathcal{D}(S)\}$. Suppose that $\dim N(T)/R(S)<\infty$.

Let $A\colon X	o Y$ and $B\colon Y	o Z$ be everywhere defined bounded linear operators, and set $\widetilde S=S+A$ and $\widetilde T=T+B$ (so $\mathcal{D}(\widetilde S)=\mathcal{D}(S)$ and $\mathcal{D}(\widetilde T)=\mathcal{D}(T)$), and assume that $R(\widetilde S)\subseteq\mathcal{D}(\widetilde T)$ and $\widetilde T\widetilde S=0$.

It is known that when $X$, $Y$, $Z$ are Hilbert spaces one has
$$\dim N(\widetilde T)/R(\widetilde S)\;=\;\dim N(T)/R(S)\;<\;\infty.$$

Does this equality continue to hold when $X$, $Y$, $Z$ are arbitrary Banach spaces?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution (positive or negative) of the Banach-space version of this stability statement for the dimension of the cohomology $N(\widetilde T)/R(\widetilde S)$ under bounded perturbations of a pair of closed operators. Related Fredholm-type stability results exist for indices of single operators under bounded/compact perturbations, but no source clearly settles this two-step Banach-space formulation. Status is therefore recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: On the perturbation of linear operators in Banach and Hilbert spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Stability theorems for closed operators under perturbations, with deficiency def A = codim R(A).
status_evidence.claim: Classical perturbation stability results exist in Banach spaces but do not directly address the two-step quotient dimension.

status_evidence.title: Sufficient Criteria for Stabilization Properties in Banach Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on stabilization properties of operators in Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to study Banach-space stability without an explicit resolution of this question.
